title: Ta-Ha, opening
hookLine: the fire, the valley, the staff (20:1–36)
carry: you are in the holy valley
tomorrow: what's a lamp doing inside a verse about God?

cards: A pile of shoes by the front door. Step out of yours and something shifts: you're inside now. Ta-Ha opens with Musa traveling at night with his family.
Far off, he sees a fire. Wait here, he tells them; maybe I can bring you a burning brand, or find guidance at the fire. He walks toward the light alone.
And a voice calls him by name. Before anything else, it tells him to take off his shoes.

teach.b: I am your Lord, the voice says; take off your shoes, for you are in the holy valley of Tuwa. Why the shoes? The surah gives the command, not the reason, and commentators offer more than one.
What it does give is the body: bare feet on holy ground, a fire in the dark.

teach.h: WHAT IS THAT IN THY RIGHT HAND?
teach.b: Then a question, almost gentle: "And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses?"
Musa answers the way anyone would, listing uses: "This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses."
God asks about a stick, and a shepherd tells Him about his stick. Then the staff becomes a gliding serpent, his hand comes out shining white, and he's sent to Pharaoh.

teach.h: LOOSEN THE KNOT IN MY TONGUE.
teach.b: So Musa asks for help: ease my heart, ease my task, loosen the knot in my tongue, and give me my brother Harun. The answer comes back: your request is granted.

Here's something to share at dinner: the Torah tells this same moment at the burning bush, in the King James words: "put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground."
Two scriptures, one barefoot man. And a hadith in Bukhari says the whole earth was made a place of prayer.

teach.h: YOU ARE IN THE HOLY VALLEY.
teach.b: A valley, a bedroom, a kitchen floor.

how: Muslims take off their shoes to enter a mosque and before praying on a prayer rug at home; prayer can be offered on any clean ground.

s: Musa took off his shoes inside a house of worship
he was in a valley, at night, walking toward a fire.
the Torah tells the shoes moment too
Exodus 3:5, at the burning bush: put off thy shoes, the place is holy ground.
the surah explains exactly why the shoes had to come off
it gives the command, not the reason; commentators offer more than one.

games.q: you have to say something hard to your dad tonight, and you're scared it'll come out wrong. what does Musa do in the same spot?
o: waits until the fear is completely gone, then goes.
asks for help: ease, a loosened tongue, and his brother beside him.
asks to be excused and sends someone braver instead.
games.why: Musa doesn't pretend to be fearless. he asks for an eased heart, a loosened tongue and Harun, and the answer is: your request is granted (20:25–36).

practice: If you can, slip off your shoes and set both feet flat on the floor. Feel what's under you, wood or tile or carpet, and the weight it's holding.
For the sit, let wherever you are be the valley: just your feet, the ground, and the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Ta-Ha. Two Arabic letters that open surah 20 and give it its name. Their meaning is left open; some take them as a name for the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

orig.note: Arabic: two letters, ta and ha, that open surah 20 and name it.

carryVoice: Carry this: you are in the holy valley, wherever your feet happen to be. See you tomorrow.
